newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude firmer, major pushes Brent higher.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude firmer, major pushes Brent higher.

text.p: Asian crude prices were slightly firmer on Friday as fears emerged of Middle East crudes trading at a discount.
In addition, the Brent market was firmer heading into the April futures expiry later on Friday.
The Brent market firmed strongly during Asian hours amid trade related to the expiry of the April Brent crude futures.
A European major bought the April/May Brent spread at 50 cents per barrel from a U.S. trader, pushing the spread out from 28 cents late in New York.
The major was also active buying Brent April partials.
Traders said the major bought three times at $19.80 per barrel.
The U.S. traders was the seller, trading sources said.
A U.S. major was heard buying a cargo of May Murban at a discount of 15 cents to ADNOC prices from a Japanese trader.
That followed trades in Oman at MPM plus two cents and then down to flat, traders said.
Traders said the economics of some of the Middle East crudes were not looking competitive versus Brent related crudes, such as West African grades.
